body.en:
Imagine a small boat floating near shore — no one rowing, no anchor dropped. It doesn't crash suddenly; it just slowly drifts further out until the shore disappears. The writer uses this picture as a warning: pay MUCH closer attention to what we've heard about Jesus, so we don't DRIFT AWAY.

If the law given through angels carried serious consequences for disobedience, how much more serious is it to ignore the salvation announced by the Lord Himself, confirmed by signs, wonders, and the Holy Spirit?

verse.en: We must pay the most careful attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

title.en: A Song for Don't Drift Away!

q.en: What warning picture does this lesson use?

en: A boat slowly drifting from shore

q.en: Why is ignoring the salvation Jesus brought so serious?

en: Because it was confirmed by the Lord Himself, signs, and the Spirit

q.en: What kind of attention does the writer say we need?

body.en:
Big idea: the danger of gradual, quiet spiritual drift — the first of five warning passages in Hebrews. Salvation is not presumed automatic; ongoing attentiveness matters.

Conversation starters: (1) What are quiet ways faith could "drift" unnoticed? (2) What helps you stay anchored? (3) Why might gradual drift be more dangerous than one big fall?

Pray for hearts that stay anchored and attentive.
